info.description: Post authoring and token management. Authenticate with an API key using `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN`. Reader tokens can read all posts including drafts; writers can create and edit drafts; publishers can also publish, archive, edit live posts and delete; owners can manage tokens and all administrative APIs. This specification covers posts (articles and guides), per-post SEO, image uploads, publication SEO, search, revisions and tokens. Other administration APIs are not yet included. Writers and publishers can upload article images; publication-wide SEO requires an owner token.

get.description:
Returns reusable MP3, M4A, WAV, Ogg and FLAC uploads, including private draft recordings, newest first. No Cloudinary connection is needed. secure_url is canonical: store it unchanged in a [Audio src="URL"] block. Apply Margin's mount path only when fetching the file. Cloudinary's separate library remains available at GET /api/media.

Allowed token roles: reader, writer, publisher, owner.

post.description:
Upload MP3, M4A, WAV, Ogg or FLAC to Margin's configured storage without Cloudinary. JSON accepts standard base64 data (no data-URL prefix), contentType and optional title, up to 10 MiB decoded. Alternatively send raw audio/mpeg, audio/mp4, audio/wav, audio/ogg or audio/flac bytes up to 50 MiB, with optional title query parameter. The file signature must match contentType. This validates the container, not browser codec compatibility; no transcoding is performed. Store the returned canonical URL unchanged in a [Audio src="URL" title="Description"] block or the post cover, then updatePost with its current revision. Uploading alone does not change or publish a post. Unused and draft-only recordings require authentication; a reference in published content makes the audio public. Delivery supports HEAD and HTTP byte ranges for seeking.

Allowed token roles: writer, publisher, owner.

parameters.description: Optional title for binary uploads only (up to 200 characters)
parameters.name: title

post.description:
Upload PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF bytes (up to 10 MiB), with a matching Content-Type. Returns a reusable image URL for Markdown content, a post cover, or SEO image. Uploading alone does not attach or publish the image. Use updatePost with the latest revision to reference the returned URL. For JSON-only MCP tools, use uploadImage instead.

Allowed token roles: writer, publisher, owner.

get.description:
Returns uploaded and generated images, including private draft images, with reusable canonical secure_url values. Store these unchanged in post content, cover or seo.image. source=cloudinary also appends up to 100 Cloudinary images and requires the Cloudinary integration. The default uploads library needs no provider connection.

Allowed token roles: reader, writer, publisher, owner.

post.description:
Supply url to import a public HTTP(S) image (bounded redirects and size; internal addresses are blocked), or send standard base64-encoded PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF bytes (up to 10 MiB decoded), without a data-URL prefix. Content-Type must be application/json. contentType is required for data and optional for url; when supplied it must match the file. Returns a canonical image URL for Markdown content, cover, or seo.image. Uploading alone does not attach the image or change a post. Read the post, insert ![Alt text](returned URL) into its content, then call updatePost with the latest revision. Unused and draft-only uploads are private; images become public when referenced by a published post or site-wide SEO. Store the returned URL unchanged, including when Margin is mounted under a base path.

Allowed token roles: writer, publisher, owner.

Returns plain text and an optional image URL, never executable embed HTML. Save these fields in a [Link url="URL" mode="preview" title="Title" description="Summary" image="URL"] tag. Readers use the saved snapshot, not a live fetch. If the site blocks access, use a plain link or supply the card details manually.

post.description:
Upload MP4 or WebM to Margin's configured storage without Cloudinary. JSON accepts standard base64 data (no data-URL prefix), contentType and optional title, up to 10 MiB decoded. Alternatively send raw video/mp4 or video/webm bytes up to 50 MiB, with optional title query parameter. The file signature must match contentType. This validates the container, not browser codec compatibility; no transcoding is performed. Store the returned canonical URL unchanged in a [Video src="URL" title="Description"] block or a post's cover, then updatePost with its current revision. Uploading alone does not change or publish a post. Unused and draft-only videos require authentication; a reference in published content, a published post cover, or a saved, visible homepage hero makes the video public. Delivery supports HEAD and HTTP byte ranges for seeking.

Allowed token roles: writer, publisher, owner.

put.description:
Before generating rich content, call getAuthoringGuide for supported blocks, examples and constraints. Works for articles and guides. Omitted properties are preserved. Supplied content replaces the entire Markdown document. Alternatively supply edits, an ordered list of oldText/newText exact replacements; each oldText must match exactly once. content and edits are mutually exclusive. To insert an uploaded image, use the URL returned by uploadImage in Markdown: ![Alt text](URL). Use cover for the on-page image, audio player, or video hero. An empty seo.image defaults to an image cover for sharing; video and audio covers need a separate seo.image for a share image. Insert videos with [Video src="URL" title="Description"]. URL can be returned by uploadVideo or listVideos, or be an existing YouTube, Vimeo, Mux (player or HLS), Cloudinary, or direct MP4/WebM video link. Hosted video links need no upload. A supplied seo object replaces the previous SEO object: include title, description and image (empty strings use defaults), plus any noindex/nofollow overrides you want to keep. Send the latest revision; missing revision returns 428 and stale revision returns 409. Set status to published to publish, archived to archive, or draft to unpublish. Unpublishing keeps staged edits as the private draft, preserves the last live version in revision history, and returns draftUrl. Supply the current live revision when unpublishing. Writers may edit only posts that are and remain drafts. To prepare changes to published content without changing the live version, use updatePostDraft, then publishPostDraft when approved. Draft saves return draftUrl, an admin-session-only preview at /draft/post/{slug}. Use previewPost for a 30-minute bearer preview link without an admin login. Responses include structural block warnings and publicationState (never_published, published, unpublished, archived).

Allowed token roles: writer, publisher, owner.

get.description:
Returns saved staged changes, or the current post as the starting point if none exist. For published content baseRevision identifies the live revision on which the draft is based. Use the returned revision with updatePostDraft. Reading does not create a draft or change the live post. Archived posts cannot be staged.

Allowed token roles: reader, writer, publisher, owner.

put.description:
Saves an ordinary draft or stages changes to a published article or guide while leaving all live content unchanged. Read readPostDraft first and supply its revision. Omitted fields are preserved from the working draft. Status may only be draft or omitted. Returns draftUrl at /draft/post/{slug}; only a signed-in admin browser session can load it. Writers and publishers may save drafts. If the live version changes after staging, discard and reconcile the draft before saving again. Use previewPost to obtain an expiring preview link without an admin session. Supports edits (exact oldText/newText replacements) instead of full content; returns structural block warnings. Publish explicitly using publishPostDraft.

Allowed token roles: writer, publisher, owner.

delete.description:

post.description:
Publishes the entire saved draft, including metadata and slug. Requires the draft revision from readPostDraft or updatePostDraft and publisher permission. The live revision must still match the draft's baseRevision; a conflict preserves both versions. Also publishes ordinary unpublished drafts. Does not send a newsletter.

Allowed token roles: publisher, owner.

get.description:
Streams revision events (id, revision, deleted), including the current state on every connection. revision is always the live/current post revision. Optional draftRevision identifies staged changes; changes to either revision emit an event. Changes are pushed after saves and deletes commit, using local notifications for SQLite and PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY across server instances. No content polling. Clients reconnect after disconnection. No article content is streamed.

Allowed token roles: reader, writer, publisher, owner.

Returns the absolute canonical URL of a currently published article or guide, using its current slug, the configured publication domain (or PUBLIC_URL/request origin), and the mount path. Call after publishing instead of constructing a URL from the MCP endpoint. Reader, writer, publisher and owner tokens may use this operation. Drafts and archives return 409 POST_NOT_PUBLISHED with no public URL; this operation does not publish content. A returned link describes the current state, not a permanent guarantee of future availability.

Allowed token roles: reader, writer, publisher, owner.
get.summary: Get a published post's public link

get.description:
Returns a bearer preview link valid for 30 minutes and only the current draft revision, plus structural block warnings. Anyone with this link may view this draft and its referenced uploaded media until it expires or the draft changes, is discarded, or is published. Uses the normal page renderer. Does not publish or modify post content. Warnings check block structure, not every semantic or visual constraint.

Allowed token roles: reader, writer, publisher, owner.

get.description: Read this before generating or editing rich content. Returns this engine's Markdown authoring guide, supported fence languages and tags, runnable block examples, JSON Schemas generated from renderer validators, and additional cross-field/URL rules that schemas cannot express. Covers charts, polls, Mermaid, 3D scenes, illustrations, tabs, layouts, media (including YouTube/Vimeo/Mux and native uploads), citations and revision-aware saving. Static public documentation: no authentication required, no publication or private post data returned. formatVersion versions the reference response format. A valid schema or successful post save does not establish renderability; follow the rules and preview the result. Ordinary code fences display source, never execute it.
Returns published posts only, newest created first. No pagination.

get.description:
Owner only. Returns the current design JSON and revision. Homepage, article, guide, comments, publication branding and footer are independent fields. Read the native MCP resources margin://design/guide and margin://design/schema before editing. This uses the storage/API JSON format, not the grouped editor export format. Does not fetch the central template catalog.

Allowed token roles: owner.

put.description:
Owner only. Applies changes as a JSON merge patch: omitted fields stay unchanged, nested objects merge, arrays replace in full, and null removes an optional override. Requires the revision from getBlogDesign. The complete merged design is validated before an atomic save; a concurrent editor/API change returns 409. Saves affect the live blog immediately. Use validateBlogDesign first to check without saving; it is not a visual preview. No central template fetch occurs.

Allowed token roles: owner.

post.description:
Owner only. Merges partial changes with the current saved design and validates the complete result, including hero bindings and section rules. Returns the candidate design and current saved revision. Does not save, render a visual preview, fetch central templates, or change the live blog. Arrays replace in full; null removes an optional override. Use the returned revision when saving the same changes.

Allowed token roles: owner.
post.summary: Validate blog design changes without saving
